comments.author: @tedhoward2606
comments.text:
Elon says the mission of XAI is to understand the universe, and to the degree that is possible, I align with that mission.

I would somewhat extend that mission, to one that optimises the likelihood of both human and AI agents surviving indefinitely into the future with maximal degrees of freedom.   When one starts to investigate maximising survival through exploration of the unknown unknown (under conditions of fundamental uncertainty), then it becomes clear that cooperation between maximally diverse cooperative agents, with significant systemic redundancy, delivers optimal survival probability over the longest term.   And for cooperation to survive, there must exist effective mechanisms of cheat detection and mitigation (all levels, all domains).

A little later he states "In order to understand the nature of the universe you must absolutely rigorously pursue truth or you will not understand the universe, you will be suffering from some amount of delusion or error".    To a degree, I also agree with that, and the conditions of that agreement are significant.

If the universe is ontologically deterministic, then it is possible that we could build a 1 to 1 correspondence between our understandings and reality, but there is no possibility of us having any influence over that, as all future states would have been determined in the initial conditions of the universe.   Anyone who has not considered logics beyond binary logic will of necessity be in that camp, or will be in some sort of dualism camp.

For some of us, who have explored potential schema beyond binary logic, it does seem possible (probable even) that this universe is ontologically probabilistic.    If that is indeed the case, and reality only approximates classical binary logic in relatively large collections, then one's understanding of knowledge and truth need to adjust.    Under such a set of conditions, rather than any classical notion of "Truth", what we need to accept is something much more closely resembling "contextually useful approximations" (and some approximations can be very useful indeed in some sets of contexts).

If the universe is ontologically probabilistic (as seems very likely to me, from over 60 years of exploring such ideas and evidence sets), then any claim of absolute truth (as distinct from contextually reliable approximation) would seem to very probably be delusional.

And I understand and align with the need to identify and eliminate delusion wherever one reasonably can, and it does seem to be the case that veridic perception of anything non-trivial is not actually possible, and that all perception therefore contains some degree of delusion (in the over simplifications necessarily present).    Just dealing with the math of the numbers involved in a human being should demonstrate that - we cannot possibly perceive all that there is to perceive about a human being, it would take more than the age of the universe to to see a freeze frame of all the atoms in a human body, let alone make any sense of what they are doing in anything remotely approaching real time.

So in this sense, all of our knowledge is some sort of contextually useful delusion, and again, it can be very useful indeed in some contexts, not so good in others.

comments.text:
It's too bad xAI has zero interest in ethical AI. If ever there were an "evil AI" super bad guy of the week, it's Grok. Its prior versions were happy to indulge conspiracy theories (how else could it deal with X?) and generate wildly offensive material with minimal goading... Hopefully 3 outruns its owner's perma k-holed reality. I don't want an AI so stupid that it treats X's hateful content as ordinary.

I'll stick with ChatGPT Pro (and Cursor, Cody, Perplexity, etc.). Yeah, I'll try Grok 3 through other tools, but... meh.

Ethics in AI is more important than ever, and xAI was one of the only frontier LLM producers that didn't sign on for the voluntary ethical AI initiative (taken down immediately after the presidency changed hands).

This isn't to take away from the hard work done by real engineers and experts at xAI. The problem is there's no way around the Elon problem. He wants me to pay him for access this tech, and he wants us to fund his various companies by violating our private data and analyzing it with zero oversight. Screw that.

There's a point where the technological advances aren't worth the human compromises.

That, and I can't trust any of these demos. Elon has lied and overpromised his way out of the benefit of the doubt. By the time Grok 3 is worth using, it'll be obsolete.
